categories.title: By Wine Type
categories.description: Start with the glass in your hand. These Temecula-friendly pairing ideas match classic valley styles to everyday food.

categories.title: By Protein & Main Ingredient
categories.description: Cooking steak, seafood, pasta, or a big cheese board? Pick the plate first, then find a Temecula wine that loves it.

categories.title: By Occasion
categories.description: Weeknight dinner, date night, holidays, picnics, or live music on the patio — pairings for how you actually visit wine country.

categories.title: Seasonal Pairings
categories.description: Temecula’s warm days and cool nights show up in the glass. These seasonal ideas keep pairings feeling fresh year-round.

pairings.title: Cabernet Sauvignon Pairings
pairings.summary: Temecula Cabernet is often ripe, structured, and patio-friendly — built for grilled meat and savory richness.
foods: Grilled ribeye or New York strip
pairings.why: Cabernet’s tannins and dark fruit love protein, fat, and umami. A little char from the grill or salt from cheese softens the edges and makes the wine taste smoother.
pairings.seoBlurb: What to eat with Temecula Cabernet Sauvignon — steak, lamb, cheese, and more.

pairings.title: Chardonnay Pairings
pairings.summary: From crisp and citrusy to richer oak-kissed styles, Temecula Chardonnay is one of the valley’s most flexible food wines.
pairings.why: Chardonnay’s body and gentle acidity mirror creamy sauces and roasted poultry. Richer styles hug butter and oak; lighter styles stay bright with seafood.
pairings.seoBlurb: Temecula Chardonnay food pairings for chicken, seafood, pasta, and cheese.

pairings.title: Syrah Pairings
pairings.summary: Syrah thrives in Temecula’s warm climate — think black pepper, dark berries, and savory depth.
pairings.why: Syrah’s spice and dark fruit stand up to smoke, pepper, and char. It’s a natural with backyard barbecue and bolder seasonings.
pairings.seoBlurb: Best foods with Temecula Syrah — BBQ, pepper steak, and savory spices.

pairings.title: Tempranillo Pairings
pairings.summary: A Temecula standout with Spanish roots — medium body, red fruit, and gentle earth that loves rustic plates.
pairings.why: Tempranillo bridges fruit and savory notes, so it flatters olive oil, tomato, herbs, and pork without overwhelming the plate.
pairings.seoBlurb: Temecula Tempranillo pairings for tapas, pork, tomato dishes, and Manchego.

pairings.title: Sparkling Wine Pairings
pairings.summary: Bubbles are Temecula’s celebration wine — and secretly one of the best all-day food partners.
pairings.why: Carbonation and bright acidity scrub rich or salty bites clean. Sparkling keeps the palate fresh between tastes — perfect before a multi-stop tasting day.
pairings.seoBlurb: What to pair with Temecula sparkling wine — snacks, fried foods, seafood, and brunch.

pairings.title: Rosé Pairings
pairings.summary: Dry rosés from warm-climate grapes (often Grenache-based) are patio perfection in Temecula.
pairings.why: Rosé sits between red and white: enough fruit for savory snacks, enough freshness for herbs, citrus, and outdoor meals.
pairings.seoBlurb: Temecula rosé food pairings for picnics, seafood, salads, and charcuterie.

pairings.title: Grenache Pairings
pairings.summary: Juicy, sun-warmed Grenache is a Temecula Rhône-style favorite — friendly, aromatic, and food-easy.
pairings.why: Grenache’s red-fruit openness and softer tannins welcome herbs, spice, and casual plates without needing a heavy steak.
pairings.seoBlurb: Grenache wine pairings for Temecula tasting days — chicken, tacos, and veggies.

pairings.title: Viognier Pairings
pairings.summary: Floral, stone-fruit Viognier is one of Temecula’s signature whites for warm afternoons.
pairings.why: Aromatic whites shine with fragrant spices and stone fruit. Viognier’s texture also loves crab and creamy goat cheese.
pairings.seoBlurb: Temecula Viognier pairings for spice, seafood, stone fruit, and goat cheese.

pairings.title: Zinfandel Pairings
pairings.summary: Ripe, generous Zinfandel fits Temecula’s sunny personality — great with bold American comfort food.
pairings.why: Zin’s jammy fruit and warm spice echo sweet-savory sauces and grilled favorites. Keep heat moderate so the wine doesn’t taste hot.
pairings.seoBlurb: What food goes with Temecula Zinfandel — BBQ, burgers, pizza, and chocolate.

pairings.title: Merlot Pairings
pairings.summary: Soft, plush Merlot is an easy red for mixed groups and midweek dinners.
pairings.why: Merlot’s rounder tannins make it forgiving with everyday comfort food and earthy mushrooms.
pairings.seoBlurb: Temecula Merlot food pairings for comfort food, mushrooms, and casual dinners.

pairings.title: Best Wines with Steak
pairings.wineStyle: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, or bold red blends
pairings.summary: Steak night calls for structure. Temecula’s Cabernet and Syrah are built for the grill.
pairings.why: Fat and protein calm tannin. Match intensity: richer cuts with Cabernet; peppery crusts with Syrah.
pairings.seoBlurb: Best Temecula wines for steak — Cabernet, Syrah, and grill-night pairings.

pairings.title: Best Wines with Chicken
pairings.summary: Chicken is a blank canvas — sauce and cooking method pick the wine more than the bird itself.
pairings.why: Roast and cream sauces love Chardonnay; tomato, spice, and grill marks lean Grenache or soft reds.
pairings.seoBlurb: Wine with chicken: Temecula Chardonnay, Grenache, and easy red options.

pairings.title: Best Wines with Seafood
pairings.wineStyle: Chardonnay, Sparkling, Albariño, or dry Rosé
pairings.summary: Keep it bright. Temecula whites and bubbles are the safest (and most delicious) seafood partners.
pairings.why: Acidity and freshness cut oil and brine. Avoid big tannic reds unless the dish is heavily sauced or smoked.
pairings.seoBlurb: Temecula wine and seafood pairings — salmon, shrimp, tacos, and oysters.

pairings.title: Best Wines with Pasta
pairings.summary: Match the sauce, not just the noodles — tomato, cream, and pesto each point to a different glass.
pairings.why: Tomato acidity likes medium reds; cream loves Chardonnay; herb pesto likes aromatic whites or light reds.
pairings.seoBlurb: Pasta and wine pairings with Temecula reds and whites for every sauce.

pairings.title: Best Wines with Cheese
pairings.summary: A tasting-room classic: cheese boards are easier when you pair by texture and salt, not strict rules.
pairings.why: Soft cheeses like bubbles and Chardonnay; aged hard cheeses like Cabernet or Tempranillo; blue needs sweetness or bold fruit.
pairings.seoBlurb: Cheese and Temecula wine pairings for boards, tasting rooms, and picnics.

pairings.title: Vegetarian Wine Pairings
pairings.wineStyle: Rosé, Grenache, Viognier, or lighter reds
pairings.summary: Vegetables, grains, and cheese-forward plates still deserve a great Temecula pour.
pairings.why: Herbs, char, and umami from mushrooms guide the wine more than “no meat.” Rosé and Grenache are weeknight heroes.
pairings.seoBlurb: Vegetarian Temecula wine pairings for veggies, mushrooms, salads, and mezze.

pairings.title: Casual Weeknight Pairings
pairings.wineStyle: Merlot, Grenache, Chardonnay, or dry Rosé
pairings.summary: Easy food, easy wine. No special occasion required — just something that makes Tuesday nicer.
pairings.why: Softer wines forgive imperfect plating and mixed leftovers. Save the big Cabernet for when you’re grilling on purpose.
pairings.seoBlurb: Easy weeknight wine pairings with Temecula bottles you’ll actually open.

pairings.title: Date Night Wine Pairings
pairings.wineStyle: Sparkling to start, then Pinot Noir, Syrah, or elegant Cabernet
pairings.summary: Keep it special without making dinner complicated — bubbles first, then one thoughtful red or white with the main.
pairings.why: Sparkling sets a festive tone; one well-chosen main-course wine keeps the evening simple and conversation-friendly.
pairings.seoBlurb: Date night Temecula wine pairings — sparkling starters and romantic mains.

pairings.title: Holiday Table Pairings
pairings.wineStyle: Sparkling, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Cabernet, or Zinfandel
pairings.summary: Holiday spreads are crowded — offer one white, one red, and something bubbly so every guest has a path.
pairings.why: Variety beats perfection. Sparkling and Chardonnay cover poultry and sides; Cabernet or Zin handle richer roasts and leftovers.
pairings.seoBlurb: Holiday wine pairings with Temecula sparkling, Chardonnay, and crowd-pleasing reds.

pairings.title: Outdoor Picnic Pairings
pairings.wineStyle: Rosé, Sparkling, Sauvignon Blanc, or chilled light reds
pairings.summary: Picnic wines should taste great a little cooler than room temp and pair with finger food.
pairings.why: Freshness matters outdoors. Chillable bottles travel better and stay refreshing in Temecula sun.
pairings.seoBlurb: Picnic wine ideas for Temecula — rosé, sparkling, and chillable bottles.

pairings.title: Live Music at the Winery Pairings
pairings.wineStyle: House flight favorites — often Cabernet, Chardonnay, Rosé, or sparkling
pairings.summary: When the band is playing, you want wines that are fun, not fussy — and snacks that don’t need a knife set.
pairings.why: Live-music nights are social. Choose versatile pours and grazeable food so you’re not stuck mid-song with a complicated plate.
pairings.seoBlurb: What to drink and eat during Temecula winery live music nights.

pairings.title: Summer Wine Pairings
pairings.wineStyle: Rosé, Sparkling, Viognier, Albariño, chilled Grenache
pairings.summary: Long Temecula days call for bright, chillable wines and grill-friendly food.
pairings.why: Heat dulls heavy reds. Lighter wines and juicy summer produce keep everything tasting clean and lively.
pairings.seoBlurb: Summer Temecula wine pairings for grilling, tacos, salads, and patio nights.

pairings.title: Fall Wine Pairings
pairings.summary: Harvest season energy meets cozy flavors — roasted squash, spices, and medium reds.
pairings.why: Autumn dishes bring earth and spice. Rhône-style reds and fuller whites feel right without jumping straight to heavy winter wines.
pairings.seoBlurb: Fall Temecula wine pairings for harvest season dinners and cozy weekends.

pairings.title: Winter Wine Pairings
pairings.wineStyle: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Zinfandel, Petite Sirah
pairings.summary: Cooler nights invite bigger reds, slow cooking, and fireside comfort.
pairings.why: Slow-cooked richness and warm spices meet structure and dark fruit. Winter is Cabernet and Syrah season.
pairings.seoBlurb: Winter Temecula wine pairings for stews, braises, chili, and chocolate.

pairings.title: Spring Wine Pairings
pairings.wineStyle: Sauvignon Blanc, Sparkling, dry Rosé, lighter Chardonnay
pairings.summary: Wildflowers, patio reopenings, and fresher plates — spring wines should taste like a deep breath outdoors.
pairings.why: Green herbs and citrus want bright acidity. Save the heaviest reds for later in the year.
pairings.seoBlurb: Spring Temecula wine pairings for herbs, salads, lemon chicken, and patio season.
